$comment: ★★ AN ORDINARY DEFINITION FOR A THREAD-LOCAL REFERENCE IS REFUSED BY NAME AT THE BINDING (P69 round 4, D-LK-THREAD-STORAGE-DISAGREEMENT-REFUSED-ONLY-BY-THE-WRITER-BACKSTOP) — the reverse of `thread_local_definition_for_an_ordinary_reference_refused`, against the same archives: ONE DSS static library per format of two members, `member_reader.c` = `extern int shared; int read_shared(void) { return shared; }` and `member_definer.c` = `int shared = 7;` (`.orchestrators/p69/work/xa/r4tls/fixtures/build_fixtures.sh`). main.c reads `extern _Thread_local int shared;`, so the archive search pulls the definer, whose definition has STATIC storage duration. C23 6.7.2p3 requires `thread_local` on every declaration of one object, and a thread-local reference reaches its object at an offset from the thread pointer, where an ordinary object has one address for the process. GNU ld 2.42 refuses the same shape ('TLS reference in ... mismatches non-TLS definition in ...'); ld.lld 18.1.3 links it, and the program faults (exit 139) (✔MEASURED 2026-10-07 on gcc 13.3.0 objects, `.orchestrators/p69/work/xa/r4probe/m10`). ✔MEASURED before this round's check, the same archives (`r4tls/fixtures/probe_examples_pre.log`): the two ELF arms were refused only by the writer's CRIT-1 backstop (`K_RelocationKindMismatch`, 'is tls-flagged but targets NON-thread-local symbol #3'); the pe64 arm by `K_SymbolUndefined` naming the reserved `_tls_index` id (D-LK-PE-THREAD-LOCAL-PROGRAM-REFUSED-BESIDE-ANY-OTHER-UNIT); and the Mach-O arm LINKED, rc 0 and no diagnostic at all — its thread-local access, a call through the variable's TLV descriptor, bound to an ordinary 4-byte object (not run: this lane's Mac did not answer). Now ONE `K_ExternImportAttributeConflict` on every arm, before the merge, naming `shared`, both units and `main`. NO `optimizedPipelines` ARM: a refusal builds no artifact for an optimized arm to differ from.
